1.title: Answer the clues
1.text: Read the clue, then type its answer into the grid. The number in a square shows where that answer starts.

2.title: Across and down
2.text: Answers run across or down and share letters where they cross, so each answer helps with the next.

3.title: Start with what you know
3.text: Some clues play with words. Fill in the ones you're sure of first; their letters will help with the rest.

1.title: Every number once
1.text: Fill the grid so each row, column and box has the numbers 1 to 4 once each. Tap a square, then a number.

2.title: A bigger grid
2.text: Now it's 1 to 6. Each box is 3 squares wide and 2 tall, and still needs every number once.

3.title: Only one place for it
3.text: Pick a number and look at a box that still needs it. Rows and columns that already have it rule squares out, and often only one is left. Stuck? Tap the bulb for a step.

1.title: Two symbols
1.text: Fill every square with one of the two symbols: tap a square to change it. Each row and column needs the same number of each, and never three the same in a line.

2.title: Spot the pairs
2.text: Two the same side by side? The squares at either end must be the other symbol. The same goes for a gap between two the same.

3.title: = and ×
3.text: An = between two squares means they're the same symbol, and an × means they're different. Use the signs with the rules you know to finish the grid.

1.title: Join A to B
1.text: Lay one track from A to B. The numbers say how many squares in each row and column have track. Tap a square to choose a piece.

2.title: Count it out
2.text: When a row or column has all its track, the rest of its squares stay empty. Use that to rule squares out.

3.title: Follow the route
3.text: Start from the stations and the piece you're given, and work out where the track must go. It never crosses itself or splits.

1.title: Build the blocks
1.text: Split the grid into rectangles. Each block covers exactly one number, and that number is how many squares it has. Drag across squares to draw a block.

2.title: Pick the shape
2.text: A 4 could be a square or a line of four. Choose a shape that doesn't cover another number.

3.title: Fill the grid
3.text: Every square must be in a block. Start with the numbers that only fit one way.

1.title: Follow the chain
1.text: Start with the number shown, then apply each step to your last answer. Type each answer on the keypad.

2.title: Work it out
2.text: Need somewhere to think? Tap the pencil to make notes. A wrong answer is marked, and you can try again.

3.title: The full chain
3.text: Eight steps, just like the daily puzzle. Take them one at a time, each from your last answer.

1.title: Every colour once
1.text: Fill the grid so each row, column and box has all four colours once. Tap a square, then a colour.

2.title: Six colours
2.text: Now there are six colours, and each box is 3 squares wide and 2 tall. Every row, column and box still needs each colour once.

3.title: Only one place for it
3.text: Pick a colour and look at a box that still needs it. Rows and columns that already have it rule squares out, and often only one is left. Stuck? Tap the bulb for a step.

1.title: Green means right
1.text: Find the hidden five-letter word in six tries. Start by typing CHAIN and pressing Enter. Green letters are right and in the right place, so keep them where they are. Grey letters aren't in the word.

2.title: Yellow means move it
2.text: Start with EARTH. Yellow letters are in the word but in the wrong place, so try them somewhere else.

3.title: Use both colours
3.text: Start with BEARD. Keep your greens where they are and move your yellows around until the word fits.

1.title: Spell with the wheel
1.text: Tap letters to make words of four letters or more, then press Enter. Every word must use the centre letter. There are five to find, and one uses every letter.

2.title: Doubles count twice
2.text: You can use each tile once per word, so a letter that's on the wheel twice can be used twice. Find the four words.

3.title: A full-size wheel
3.text: Five words to find. Plurals don't count. Stuck? Shuffle the letters to see them in a new way.

1.title: Find the words
1.text: Drag from the first letter of a word to its last. Here the words read across or down. Find the three in the list.

2.title: Any direction
2.text: Words can also run backwards or diagonally. Find all four.

3.title: A bigger grid
3.text: Six words hiding in every direction. Stuck? Tap a word in the list to see its first letter.

1.title: Numbers are letters
1.text: Each number stands for one letter, and the same number is always the same letter. T, I, L and E are done for you. Fill in the rest to finish the words.

2.title: Same number, same letter
2.text: When a number appears twice in a row, so does its letter, like the double E and double T here. Use them to finish the words.

3.title: Start with what you know
3.text: Words with most of their letters filled in are the easiest to crack. Start with those, then use each new letter to finish the rest.
